newsitem.title: EL SALVADOR: In El Salvador, arms are traded for food and goods.
newsitem.headline: In El Salvador, arms are traded for food and goods.

text.p: Civilians in El Salvador have turned in 4,277 weapons in exchange for $575,000 worth of food and household goods, organisers of an arms-for-goods programme said on Tuesday.
The exchange was a private initiative aiming to bring peace to one of Central America's most violent societies.

Organisers told reporters they rounded up 1,340 assault rifles including M-16s, AK-47s, AR-15s, Galils and G-3s as well as 718 handguns, 1,334 grenades, 167 rockets, 18 grenade launchers and 52,693 rounds of ammunition on Sunday.
The Patriotic Movement Against Delinquency also collected 105 pounds (48 kg) of TNT, 79 pounds (36 kg) of plastic explosives and a host of other weapons, movement leader David Gutierrez said.
The movement has organised several such swaps, in which people receive food and other basic household goods in exchange for arms. Each handgun is worth $172 in coupons, and each rifle is worth $345.
The weapons were collected at various churches throughout the country. Many were left over from El Salvador's 12-year-old civil war, which ended in 1992.
